t: A Nguni kingdom built by the Dlamini dynasty under Sobhuza I and Mswati II, the king after whom the Swazi are named.
The king (Ngwenyama) rules alongside the queen mother (Ndlovukati), and kingship is renewed each year in the Incwala.
After concessions, Boer and British rule, it regained independence in 1968 and remains one of the world’s last absolute monarchies.
dyk: Sobhuza II reigned from 1899, when he was a few months old, until 1982, one of the longest reigns of any monarch in recorded history.
ev: The Dlamini under Ngwane III settle near the lower Pongola river
Sobhuza I moves north to the Ezulwini valley under Ndwandwe pressure
Mswati II begins his reign and builds the age-regiment system
Swaziland becomes a protectorate of the South African Republic
The Partition Proclamation leaves the Swazi only about a third of their land
Swaziland becomes independent under Sobhuza II
Sobhuza II repeals the constitution and bans political parties
Mswati III renames the country the Kingdom of Eswatini

f.capital: Royal villages of the Ezulwini valley; later Lobamba (royal and legislative) and Mbabane (administrative)
